literal: Yuan Tan; Yuan Bin; Yuan Xiaoyou; Yuan Huiye; Yuan Bi; Yuan Shao
idiomatic: Yuan Tan; Yuan Bin; Yuan Xiaoyou; Yuan Huiye; Yuan Bi; Yuan Shao

literal: Yuan Tan — his grandfather was Emperor Xianwen of Wei; seventh son of Prince Xianyang Xi.
idiomatic: Yuan Tan's grandfather was Emperor Xianwen of Wei; he was the seventh son of Prince Xianyang Xi.

literal: After Xi was executed, his elder brothers Yi, Shu, and five others fled south in succession, so Tan was able to inherit; his fief was changed to Prince of Fucheng.
idiomatic: After Xi was executed, his elder brothers Yi, Shu, and five others fled south one after another, so Tan inherited the title; his fief was changed to prince of Fucheng.

literal: At the beginning of Yong'an he was restored to his original enfeoffment as Prince of Xianyang commandery; he rose through repeated promotions to palace attendant.
idiomatic: At the beginning of Yong'an he was restored to his original enfeoffment as prince of Xianyang commandery and rose through repeated promotions to palace attendant.

literal: Emperor Zhuang said to him at ease: ""Prince, your talent is not like Xun or Cai; in your middle years you have been repeatedly transferred — this must be because you grew up young in my household, hence the extraordinary promotions.
idiomatic: Emperor Zhuang said to him at ease, "Prince, your talent is not like that of Xun or Cai; yet in mid-career you have been repeatedly promoted. That must be because you grew up in my household from youth — hence these extraordinary appointments.

literal: " Earlier, after Xi died his sons were impoverished; Tan and his brothers were taken in and raised by Prince Pengcheng Xie — hence this remark.
idiomatic: " Earlier, after Xi died his sons were impoverished; Tan and his brothers were taken in and raised by Prince Pengcheng Xie — hence this remark.

literal: At the beginning of Emperor Xiaowu's reign, his elder brother Shu was captured.
idiomatic: At the beginning of Emperor Xiaowu's reign, his elder brother Shu was captured.

literal: Tan saw that Shu was both older and worthy, and feared Shu would replace him; he secretly urged the court to eliminate Shu by law.
idiomatic: Tan saw that Shu was older and more worthy and feared he would be displaced; he secretly urged the court to eliminate Shu by law.

literal: When Shu learned of it, he wept at the Wei River and said to Tan: "I once, because of family calamity, could not die; I lived on others' food on rivers and lakes and accepted their ranks and commands.
idiomatic: When Shu learned of it, he wept on the Wei River and said to Tan, "Long ago, because of our family's calamity, I could not die; I lived on others' food along rivers and lakes and accepted their ranks and commands.

literal: My coming now is not from righteousness — I seek only to live; how could I hope for glory.
idiomatic: My coming now is not from righteousness — I seek only to live. How could I hope for glory?

literal: Why do you indulge your suspicions and forget the bond of kin from one root? Though your back and waist are imposing, your goodness is nothing worth praising.
idiomatic: Why do you indulge your suspicions and forget the bond of those from one root? Though your back and waist are imposing, there is no goodness in you worth praising.

literal: " Tan flushed and left.
idiomatic: " Tan flushed and left.

literal: When Shu died, Tan never went to mourn at his coffin.
idiomatic: When Shu died, Tan never went to mourn at his coffin.

literal: Tan held the posts of Minister over the Masses, Grand Commandant, and Grand Tutor, with additional posts as palace attendant, grand preceptor, recorder of the masters of writing, director of imperial clan affairs, and governor of Sizhou.
idiomatic: Tan served as minister over the masses, grand commandant, and grand tutor, with additional posts as palace attendant, grand preceptor, recorder of the masters of writing, director of imperial clan affairs, and governor of Sizhou.

literal: Though his salary was rich and his rank exalted, his greed grew ever worse; he sold judgments and traded offices without limit.
idiomatic: Though his salary was rich and his rank exalted, his greed grew ever worse; he sold judgments and traded offices without limit.

literal: The censorate impeached him and he was dismissed from office; he returned to his estate as a prince.
idiomatic: The censorate impeached him and he was dismissed; he returned to his estate as a prince.

literal: Soon he was recalled as special eminence, sent out as inspector of Jizhou, and again devoted himself to extortion.
idiomatic: Soon he was recalled as special eminence and sent out as inspector of Jizhou, where he again devoted himself to extortion.

literal: Whenever the common people paid taxes, aside from the regular tax he first exacted an extra five bolts of silk, and only then would accept payment.
idiomatic: Whenever the common people paid taxes, aside from the regular levy he first exacted five extra bolts of silk per household, and only then would accept payment.

literal: He loved hunting and fishing; not a day passed without going out — in autumn and winter he hunted pheasants and hares, in spring and summer he caught fish and crabs; his hawks and dogs numbered in the hundreds.
idiomatic: He loved hunting and fishing and went out every day without exception — in autumn and winter he hunted pheasants and hares, in spring and summer he caught fish and crabs; his hawks and dogs numbered in the hundreds.

literal: He said himself that he would rather go three days without food than one day without hunting.
idiomatic: He said himself that he would rather go three days without food than one day without hunting.

literal: He entered court as grand tutor.
idiomatic: He entered court as grand tutor.

literal: At the beginning of Qi Tianbao, per precedent his rank was reduced; he was enfeoffed Duke of Xinfeng county and appointed special eminence and commissioner with credentials equal to the Three Dukes.
idiomatic: At the beginning of Tianbao under Qi, per precedent his rank was reduced; he was enfeoffed duke of Xinfeng county and appointed special eminence and commissioner with credentials equal to the Three Dukes.

literal: Because his son Shibao and the attendant cavalier attendant-in-ordinary Peng Guiping, in drunkenness, slandered and rashly spoke of portents and prophecy, the authorities memorialized that they should die; an edict pardoned them both.
idiomatic: Because his son Shibao and the attendant cavalier attendant-in-ordinary Peng Guiping, while drunk, slandered the court and rashly spoke of portents and prophecy, the authorities memorialized that they should die; an edict pardoned them both.

literal: Tan was consigned to northern Yingzhou; he died in the place of his assignment.
idiomatic: Tan was consigned to northern Yingzhou and died in the place of his assignment.

literal: Yuan Bin, styled Shanjii, his grandfather was Emperor Xianwen of Wei.
idiomatic: Yuan Bin, styled Shanjii — his grandfather was Emperor Xianwen of Wei.

literal: His father Prince Gaoyang Yong followed Emperor Xiaozhuang at Heyin and met disaster there.
idiomatic: His father Prince Gaoyang Yong followed Emperor Xiaozhuang to Heyin and met disaster there.

literal: Bin in youth inherited his grandfather's title; he held posts including palace attendant and left vice director of the masters of writing.
idiomatic: Bin in youth inherited his grandfather's title and held posts including palace attendant and left vice director of the masters of writing.

literal: Bin had fine appearance; his nature was mild and broad; in office he was cautious and weighty — Gao Cheng greatly loved and appreciated him.
idiomatic: Bin had fine looks; his nature was mild and broad; in office he was cautious and weighty — Gao Cheng greatly loved and appreciated him.

literal: At the beginning of Qi Tianbao, per precedent his rank was reduced; he became Duke of Gaoyang county and was appointed right grand master for the brilliant.
idiomatic: At the beginning of Tianbao under Qi, per precedent his rank was reduced; he became duke of Gaoyang county and was appointed right grand master for the brilliant.

literal: In the second year, returning from campaigning against the Khitan with Emperor Wenxuan, at the Bailang River he was ordered to die for his crime.
idiomatic: In the second year, returning from campaigning against the Khitan with Gao Yang, at the Bailang River he was ordered to die for his crime.

literal: Yuan Xiaoyou — his grandfather was Emperor Taiwu of Wei.
idiomatic: Yuan Xiaoyou — his grandfather was Emperor Taiwu of Wei.

literal: His elder brother Prince Huaihuai Yu had no son; he had Xiaoyou inherit the title.
idiomatic: His elder brother Prince Huaihuai Yu had no son; Xiaoyou was made to inherit the title.

literal: He rose through repeated promotions to inspector of Cangzhou; his governance was mild and harmonious, he liked to do small favors; he could not be upright but did not violate or harass others — the common people found this convenient.
idiomatic: He rose through repeated promotions to inspector of Cangzhou; his governance was mild and harmonious, and he liked to do small favors. He could not be upright, yet he did not violate or harass others — the common people found this convenient.

literal: Emperor Jing of Wei feasted Gao Cheng at Hualin; Xiaoyou, drunk, praised himself, and also said: "Your Majesty promised to grant me ability.
idiomatic: Emperor Jing of Wei feasted Gao Cheng at Hualin; Xiaoyou, drunk, praised himself and also said, "Your Majesty promised to grant me ability.

literal: " The Emperor laughed and said: "I constantly hear the Prince speak of his own integrity.
idiomatic: " The emperor laughed and said, "I constantly hear the Prince speak of his own integrity.

literal: " Gao Cheng said: "Prince Huaihuai received the decree and is pardoned of guilt.
idiomatic: " Gao Cheng said, "Prince Huaihuai has received the decree and is pardoned of guilt.

literal: " Thereupon ruler and ministers all laughed and did not punish him.
idiomatic: " Thereupon ruler and ministers all laughed and did not punish him.

literal: Xiaoyou was clear in governing principles; he once submitted a memorial saying:
idiomatic: Xiaoyou was skilled in governance; he once submitted a memorial that read:

literal: The present system: a hundred households form a party-chief group; twenty households a lane; five households a neighboring unit.
idiomatic: The present system: a hundred households form a party-chief group; twenty households a lane; five households a neighboring unit.

literal: Within a hundred households there are twenty-five chiefs exempt from levies — joy and suffering are uneven.
idiomatic: Within a hundred households there are twenty-five chiefs exempt from levies — joy and suffering fall unevenly.

literal: Few sheep and many wolves — moreover there is nibbling away.
idiomatic: Few sheep and many wolves — and on top of that, nibbling away.

literal: That this is harmful has been long.
idiomatic: That this is harmful has been so for a long time.

literal: In the capital's wards, some seven or eight hundred households have only one lane chief and two clerks, yet nothing is wanting in daily affairs — how much more so in the outer provinces?
idiomatic: In the capital's wards, some seven or eight hundred households have only one lane chief and two clerks, yet daily affairs suffer no lack — how much more so in the outer provinces?

literal: I request that the old name of Three Chiefs be kept unchanged, but a hundred households form a clan, four lanes, two neighboring units per lane.
idiomatic: I request that the old name of Three Chiefs be kept unchanged, but a hundred households form a clan, with four lanes and two neighboring units per lane.

literal: Calculated, a clan has twelve fewer adult males — obtaining twelve bolts of compensatory silk.
idiomatic: By the reckoning, each clan has twelve fewer adult males liable for service — yielding twelve bolts of compensatory silk.

literal: Roughly calculated, the households under management should be over twenty thousand clans; in one year that yields two hundred forty thousand bolts of compensatory silk.
idiomatic: Roughly calculated, the households under management should exceed twenty thousand clans; in one year that yields two hundred forty thousand bolts of compensatory silk.

literal: Fifteen adult males form one rotation of soldiers — calculating, one obtains sixteen thousand troops.
idiomatic: Fifteen adult males form one rotation of soldiers — by the reckoning, one obtains sixteen thousand troops.

literal: This is the way to enrich the state and settle the people.
idiomatic: This is the way to enrich the state and settle the people.

literal: In antiquity feudal lords married nine women; a gentleman one wife and one concubine.
idiomatic: In antiquity feudal lords married nine women; a gentleman took one wife and one concubine.

literal: "Jin ordinance": princes may set up eight concubines;
idiomatic: The Jin ordinance: princes may set up eight concubines;

literal: commandery marquises and marquises, six concubines.
idiomatic: commandery marquises and marquises, six concubines.

literal: "Office-rank ordinance": first and second ranks four concubines, third and fourth three, fifth and sixth two, seventh and eighth one.
idiomatic: The office-rank ordinance: first and second ranks four concubines, third and fourth three, fifth and sixth two, seventh and eighth one.

literal: thereby the woman's instruction is thoroughly cultivated and succession broadly provided.
idiomatic: Thus the instruction of women is thoroughly cultivated and succession broadly provided for.

literal: Broad succession is filial; cultivating woman's instruction is ritual.
idiomatic: Broad succession is filial; cultivating women's instruction is ritual.

literal: But the sage court suddenly abandoned these numbers; for long it has gradually worsened; generals and ministers mostly honor princesses in marriage, kings and marquises marry empress-clan women — hence no concubines; it has become customary.
idiomatic: But the sage court suddenly abandoned these numbers; for a long time it has gradually worsened. Generals and ministers mostly take princesses in marriage; kings and marquises marry empress-clan women — hence there are no concubines, and it has become customary.

literal: Alas for women — born unlucky in this age: the whole court is without concubines; under Heaven nearly all have one wife.
idiomatic: Women are unfortunate to be born in this age: the whole court is without concubines, and under Heaven nearly everyone has but one wife.

literal: Suppose one with strong will took many wives — then the household would scatter, one's affairs would go badly, and kinsmen inside and out would together mock and wonder.
idiomatic: Suppose someone of strong will took many wives — then the household would scatter, his affairs would go badly, and kinsmen inside and out would together mock and wonder.

literal: People today universally lack standards.
idiomatic: People today universally lack standards.

literal: When parents marry off daughters they teach jealousy; aunts and sisters in welcoming them surely urge mutual suspicion.
idiomatic: When parents marry off daughters they teach jealousy; aunts and sisters, in welcoming them, surely urge mutual suspicion.

literal: To control the husband is taken as wifely virtue; to be able to be jealous is taken as woman's craft.
idiomatic: To control the husband is taken as wifely virtue; to be able to be jealous is taken as woman's craft.

literal: They say themselves they will not be bullied by others — they fear others will laugh at them.
idiomatic: They say themselves they will not be bullied by others — they fear others will laugh at them.

literal: Kings and dukes even so keep but one heart — how dare those below have two minds?
idiomatic: Even kings and dukes keep but one heart — how dare those below have two minds?

literal: When jealous suspicion arises, the rites between wife and concubines are abandoned; when those rites are abandoned, omens of licentiousness arise — this is what your servant bitterly hates.
idiomatic: When jealous suspicion arises, the rites between wife and concubines are abandoned; when those rites are abandoned, omens of licentiousness arise — this is what your servant bitterly hates.

literal: I request that for first-rank kings and dukes they marry eight, with the principal wife to complete nine women, as befits the office.
idiomatic: I request that first-rank kings and dukes marry eight concubines, with the principal wife completing nine women in all, as befits the office.

literal: Second rank seven; third and fourth five; fifth and sixth one wife and two concubines.
idiomatic: Second rank, seven; third and fourth ranks, five; fifth and sixth ranks, one wife and two concubines.

literal: Limited to one year, all are ordered to fill the number.
idiomatic: Within one year, all are ordered to fill the number.

literal: If they do not fill the number, or keep concubines improperly, or let the wife in jealousy add beating — dismiss them from the office they hold.
idiomatic: If they do not fill the number, or keep concubines improperly, or let the wife in jealousy add beatings — dismiss them from the office they hold.

literal: If the wife has no son and will not take a concubine, that is self-extinction — no blood-offering to ancestors — I request penalize with the crime of unfilial piety and divorce the wife.
idiomatic: If the wife has no son and will not take a concubine, that is self-extinction — no blood-offering to ancestors. I request they be penalized with the crime of unfilial piety and the wife divorced and sent away.

literal: Your servant's loyal heart, in righteousness, is only for family and state; I wish to make auspicious and inauspicious all conform to ritual, noble and base each have their proper place, reduce chief-leaders to levy soldiers, establish granaries to fill grain stores, set reward regulations to capture thieves and rebels, execute canonical statutes to display court regulations — perhaps thereby sufficient food and sufficient arms, and the people will trust.
idiomatic: Your servant's loyal heart, in righteousness, is only for family and state. I wish to make the auspicious and inauspicious all conform to ritual, noble and base each have their proper place, reduce chief-leaders to levy soldiers, establish granaries to fill grain stores, set reward regulations to capture thieves and rebels, and execute canonical statutes to display the court's regulations — so that there may be sufficient food and sufficient arms, and the people will trust.

literal: Again I rashly petition concerning the number of wives and concubines — my true aim is to make the sons and grandsons of kings, marquises, generals, ministers, and meritorious ministers fill the court with flourishing heirs, and transmission of the throne without end.
idiomatic: Again I rashly petition concerning the number of wives and concubines — my true aim is to make the sons and grandsons of kings, marquises, generals, ministers, and meritorious ministers fill the court with flourishing heirs, so that the transmission of the throne may be without end.
